items.text:
Yep — this mismatch is **not you going insane**. It happens because:

- In the editor, your slot text is short (`Slot — EMPTY`) → cards stay the intended width.
- In-game, your script sets **long text** (`Slot 1 — Profile 1 (Runs: 0) ...`) → **Label minimum size tries to grow** → Grid tries to accommodate → shit spills / clips / looks “different”.

Also, the way we did “Select is the parent Button” makes layout/min-size behavior weirder than it needs to be.

### Fix: make the card a fixed-size Control + clip the text
This makes runtime look exactly like the editor **no matter how long the text is**.

---

## 1) Replace `res://ui/SaveCard.tscn` with THIS (important)
This version:
- Root is **Control** with fixed minimum size (so text can’t blow the grid wide).
- Content is in a normal container (so layout behaves).
- A `Select` button sits **behind** visuals, and the visuals don’t block clicks.
- Name label **clips + ellipsis** instead of expanding the card.

Result: **`GridContainer` has 0 children → your script explodes**.

The clean fix (and way easier to maintain): **make one reusable “SaveCard” scene** and instance it 3 times in the grid. That prevents this copy/paste-parent-path hell entirely.

Below are **exact files** to paste.

Now `GridContainer` will **always** have 3 children (Card1–Card3), no more orphan spam.

---

# 3) Replace `res://ui/SaveSelect.gd` with this (matches the new structure)

```gdscript
extends Control

@onready var title: Label = $VBoxContainer/Title
@onready var grid: GridContainer = $VBoxContainer/GridContainer
@onready var back: Button = $VBoxContainer/Back

const SLOT_COUNT := 3

func _ready() -> void:
	get_tree().paused = false
	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS

	title.text = "Select Save"
	back.pressed.connect(func(): get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://ui/MainMenu.tscn"))

	_wire_buttons()
	_refresh_ui()

func _card(slot: int) -> Control:
	return grid.get_child(slot - 1) as Control

func _select_btn(slot: int) -> Button:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select") as Button

func _name_label(slot: int) -> Label:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select/Content/VBox/Name") as Label

func _delete_btn(slot: int) -> Button:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select/Content/VBox/Buttons/Delete") as Button

func _rename_btn(slot: int) -> Button:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select/Content/VBox/Buttons/Rename") as Button

func _wire_buttons() -> void:
	for slot in range(1, SLOT_COUNT + 1):
		var select_b := _select_btn(slot)
		var del_b := _delete_btn(slot)
		var ren_b := _rename_btn(slot)

		select_b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
		del_b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
		ren_b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE

		select_b.pressed.connect(func(): _on_slot_pressed(slot))
		del_b.pressed.connect(func(): _on_delete_pressed(slot))
		ren_b.pressed.connect(func(): _on_rename_pressed(slot))

func _refresh_ui() -> void:
	for slot in range(1, SLOT_COUNT + 1):
		var s = SaveManager.load_slot(slot)
		var name_l := _name_label(slot)

		if s == null:
			name_l.text = "Slot %d — EMPTY (click to create)" % slot
		else:
			name_l.text = "Slot %d — %s (Runs: %d)" % [slot, s.profile_name, s.total_runs]

func _on_slot_pressed(slot: int) -> void:
	var s = SaveManager.load_slot(slot)
	if s == null:
		s = SaveManager.create_slot(slot, "Profile %d" % slot)

	SaveManager.set_current(slot, s)
	get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://ui/Base.tscn")

func _on_delete_pressed(slot: int) -> void:
	SaveManager.delete_slot(slot)
	_refresh_ui()

func _on_rename_pressed(slot: int) -> void:
	var s = SaveManager.load_slot(slot)
	if s == null:
		return
	s.profile_name = "Renamed %d" % slot
	SaveManager.save_slot(s)
	_refresh_ui()
```

---

## One important instruction so it doesn’t “fuck itself” again
Don’t paste these big `.tscn` blocks into the **scene tree**.  
Paste them into the **actual file contents** (Godot’s text editor view of the `.tscn`, or external editor), save, then reopen the scene.

---

If you want, next step: I can help you wire the `Preview` TextureRect to show the last run screenshot per save slot (or a placeholder image if empty).

1) **Title**: easy, we’ll add it back cleanly.
2) That error means **your `GridContainer` has 0 children at runtime** → i.e. the three cards are not actually under it in the scene you’re running (most common causes: you didn’t paste/save the updated `.tscn`, or you’re accidentally running a different SaveSelect scene).

I’ll give you:
- a tiny **.tscn add** for the title
- a **SaveSelect.gd** that matches your new card structure **and won’t crash** (it will print what’s wrong if the grid is empty)

---

## 1) Add the title label back into `SaveSelect.tscn`
In your `SaveSelect.tscn`, under:

- `VBoxContainer`
  - `SpacerTop`

Add this **right after `SpacerTop`**:

```gdscript
[node name="Title" type="Label" parent="VBoxContainer"]
layout_mode = 2
text = "Select Save"
horizontal_alignment = 1
theme_override_font_sizes/font_size = 28
```

So your VBox order becomes:
`SpacerTop -> Title -> GridContainer -> Back -> SpacerBottom`

---

## 2) Replace `SaveSelect.gd` with this (correct paths + grid-empty guard)
Paste this over your whole script:

```gdscript
extends Control

@onready var title: Label = $VBoxContainer/Title
@onready var grid: GridContainer = $VBoxContainer/GridContainer
@onready var back: Button = $VBoxContainer/Back

const SLOT_COUNT := 3

func _ready() -> void:
	get_tree().paused = false
	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS

	title.text = "Select Save"

	back.pressed.connect(func():
		get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://ui/MainMenu.tscn")
	)

	# If the grid is being populated later for some reason, wait 1 frame.
	await get_tree().process_frame

	print("SAVE SELECT READY:", scene_file_path)
	print("Grid child count:", grid.get_child_count())

	if grid.get_child_count() < SLOT_COUNT:
		push_error("SaveSelect: GridContainer has %d cards, expected %d. Your SaveSelect.tscn probably isn't the updated one (or the cards aren't parented under GridContainer)." % [grid.get_child_count(), SLOT_COUNT])
		return

	_wire_buttons()
	_refresh_ui()

func _card(slot: int) -> Control:
	return grid.get_child(slot - 1) as Control

func _select_btn(slot: int) -> Button:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select") as Button

func _name_label(slot: int) -> Label:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select/MarginContainer/VBoxContainer/Name") as Label

func _delete_btn(slot: int) -> Button:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select/MarginContainer/VBoxContainer/HBoxContainer/Delete") as Button

func _rename_btn(slot: int) -> Button:
	return _card(slot).get_node("Select/MarginContainer/VBoxContainer/HBoxContainer/Rename") as Button

func _wire_buttons() -> void:
	for slot in range(1, SLOT_COUNT + 1):
		var select_b := _select_btn(slot)
		var del_b := _delete_btn(slot)
		var ren_b := _rename_btn(slot)

		select_b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
		del_b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
		ren_b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE

		select_b.pressed.connect(func(): _on_slot_pressed(slot))
		del_b.pressed.connect(func(): _on_delete_pressed(slot))
		ren_b.pressed.connect(func(): _on_rename_pressed(slot))

func _refresh_ui() -> void:
	for slot in range(1, SLOT_COUNT + 1):
		var s = SaveManager.load_slot(slot)
		var name_l := _name_label(slot)

		if s == null:
			name_l.text = "Slot %d — EMPTY (click to create)" % slot
		else:
			name_l.text = "Slot %d — %s (Runs: %d)" % [slot, s.profile_name, s.total_runs]

func _on_slot_pressed(slot: int) -> void:
	var s = SaveManager.load_slot(slot)
	if s == null:
		s = SaveManager.create_slot(slot, "Profile %d" % slot)

	SaveManager.set_current(slot, s)
	get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://ui/Base.tscn")

func _on_delete_pressed(slot: int) -> void:
	SaveManager.delete_slot(slot)
	_refresh_ui()

func _on_rename_pressed(slot: int) -> void:
	var s = SaveManager.load_slot(slot)
	if s == null:
		return
	s.profile_name = "Renamed %d" % slot
	SaveManager.save_slot(s)
	_refresh_ui()
```

## Why you got “Index out of bounds”
That message means:

`grid.get_child_count() == 0`

So `grid.get_child(0)` explodes.

With the script above, you’ll now see a clear `push_error()` telling you exactly that — **and it’ll print the scene path** so you can confirm you’re running the file you edited.

If you run it and it prints `Grid child count: 0`, the fix is **100% in the scene**: open `SaveSelect.tscn` and make sure the three `PanelContainer` nodes are actually children of `GridContainer` (not accidentally moved elsewhere), and that you saved the file.

If you want, paste the *top of your scene tree* (just the node list from the editor) and I’ll tell you immediately where they ended up.
